Honda Plots Radical Makeover, All-New Accord SUV Coming in 2029
7 photos
Photo: Honda
One of America's favorite sedans (not so many left, anyway!) is inching closer to a major refresh, which is expected to drop the conventional sedan look and bring a futuristic makeover. The new Accord is expected to hit the market in the second half of 2027 as a 2028 model with a yet-undisclosed price bump.
The Honda Accord has been in the Japanese automaker’s portfolio since May 7, 1976. A month later, it debuted in North America as a 1977 model year . The Accord started out in life as a three-door hatchback before being rolled out also as a sedan.
So it has been on the market for half a century, and it looks like it is not going anywhere. However, after 11 generations, 25 million examples sold worldwide, and 15 million sold in the United States, the model is set to transform.
Scrap what you know about the Honda Accord’s design. Launched back in 2022 as a 2023 model year, the Accord is set to undergo restyling. Its current look will vanish into thin air with the major update. Rather than leaning into the current conservative look, the upcoming Accord will get aggressive and sporty, thus shifting toward a new segment of buyers.
Photo: Honda The redesign is expected to be "modern and futuristic," as people familiar with the matter told Automotive News. The future Accord will reportedly draw heavily from Honda’s wedge-shaped 0 Series lineup, which the automaker almost entirely canceled as a radical effect of the EV market meltdown and low profitability estimates. The future Accord will also steal design cues from the recently unveiled low-slung Hybrid Sedan Prototype.
The Accord will trade its large front grille for a much narrower one, flanked by razor-thin, aggressive LED headlights and restyled lower air intakes. The model is expected to get a wider, lower stance and a sweeping fastback Grand Tourer roofline. In the meantime, a sleek, full-width LED light bar will split the rear end in two. The trunk lid will get an integrated trunk lip spoiler.
Honda is also preparing a major overhaul for the cabin. A driver-focused, premium layout, featuring a wider, floating central infotainment screen, is part of the plan, along with a fully digital instrument cluster. Google built-in with Gemini integration and over-the-air software updates will also be on the menu.
The upcoming Accord is also expected to receive the simulated S+ Shift system, which debuted back in September 2025 with the Prelude and is specifically designed for hybrid vehicles, as it relies solely on the electric motor to simulate gear shifts.
Photo: Theottle | YouTube Speaking of powertrain, the refreshed Accord, still sitting on an updated version of the Honda Global Architecture, is expected to debut an advanced two-motor hybrid system, supposedly pairing either the 1.5-liter inline-four or the 2.0-liter direct-injection Atkinson cycle engine with updated electric drive tech, aiming for over a 10% improvement in fuel economy.
The starting price is anticipated to stay competitive, kicking off around $30,000. Right now, the 2026 Accord starts at $28,395 before options and fees, and is available in six distinct trims. The lineup starts with the base LX and goes all the way to the range-topping Touring Hybrid, which is a $39,495 deal.
Honda’s long-term plans include rolling out an Accord SUV with a lifted, wagon-like body style by mid-2029 to rival the Subaru Outback, as reported by Motor1. That is when the Accord should become an all-hybrid lineup, powered by newly developed four-cylinder engines, set to replace the current 1.5- and 2.0-liter units.
The SUV would go into production at Honda’s Marysville, Ohio, plant, alongside a new generation of the Accord sedan , which will be underpinned by a new architecture. With almost its entire North American EV lineup canceled back in March, Honda is re-routing its resources toward rolling out hybrids.
Honda Accord, one of America’s best-selling sedans As the affordable sedan segment is slowly dying, the Honda Accord is still one of America’s favorites, but it is obviously struggling to keep up with the rivals. Honda sold 150,196 units in 2025 and 145,521 units so far in 2026, which means it is comfortably on track to shatter last year's total.
Photo: Honda By maintaining its current monthly sales average through Q4, the Accord is projected to finish 2026 with roughly 194,000 total deliveries. This pace represents a massive ~29% full-year sales surge, marking the Accord's strongest annual performance in years.
In the meantime, the Toyota Camry holds onto its crown, having sold 260,684 examples from January to September this year. Toyota’s rock-solid dominance is confirmed by the Corolla, which comes in second, with 195,000 cars moved, while the Honda Civic stands third with 180,000 cars in the first nine months of the year.
Honda is well aware that it has to roll out affordable vehicles if it wants to stay competitive in the segment. This means that the future Accord SUV will have to sit at around $35,000. That is where rival, the Subaru Outback , is at.
